objective.name: sandbox.dsl.parallel.mix
objective.description: Bounded-parallel DSL flow mixing local wrapper, remote engine-native, and remote wrapper-backed subcalls.

#root.role: Run three awaited subcalls with bounded concurrency and return one aggregated payload.

effects.local_wrapper_runtime: The local wrapper runtime is invoked.
effects.external_route: Remote engine-native and remote wrapper-backed routes cross the inter-instance boundary.

transformation_contract.morphing: A local DSL request becomes one aggregated response after bounded concurrent orchestration of local and remote sub-capacities.
invariants: The flow launches exactly three awaited subcalls under a parallel concurrency limit of 2.
The aggregated terminal payload is built from all successful parallel branches.
No branch-specific response becomes terminal on its own while the parallel group succeeds.
success: On success, the terminal payload is the runtime parallel aggregation of the local wrapper branch, the remote state branch, and the remote wrapper branch.
Successful execution proves bounded parallel orchestration across local and inter-instance subcalls.
failure: The flow fails terminally if any required parallel branch fails under the default fail policy.
A failure in one branch prevents the parallel aggregate from becoming a successful terminal payload.
notes: This scenario is the baseline N7 proof for bounded parallel composition.
The concurrency limit is part of the scenario semantics, not just an optimization detail.
